{{Quote|With the Force there are two paths&mdash;good and evil&mdash;one may take, nothing in-between. One leads to a full life, no matter the years. Justice, knowledge and compassion are both endeavors and rewards. The other is most assuredly a short path that leads to untamed power. With nothing to earn, it leads to a certain solitary end. One should choose wisely.|Qu Rahn|<ref name="DF II game manual">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]'' game manual</ref>}}
'''Qu Rahn''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] native of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Socorro/Legends|Socorro]] who served the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during its waning [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. When the Republic was reformed into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] and the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] began, Rahn went into hiding, evading numerous Imperial [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitors]]. At some point during the Purge, Rahn visited his former Jedi Master, [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], from whom he learned the secret of living as a [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghost]] after physical [[Death/Legends|death]]. Elevating Rahn to the rank of Jedi Master, Yoda also told him about the long-lost [[Valley of the Jedi]], a powerful [[Vergence/Legends|Force nexus]] which contained numerous trapped Jedi souls. Rahn swore to find it and free the spirits, but after many years of obsessive and fruitless search, he almost gave up.

A [[Force vision/Legends|vision]] led Rahn to a common farmer called [[Morgan Katarn]], who had accidentally stumbled upon the Valley. Having foreseen that he would soon be captured, Rahn instructed Morgan to pass the information about the Valley to his son, [[Kyle Katarn|Kyle]]. During this time period, Qu Rahn eventually joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] during the early years of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], being one of the few Jedi left in the galaxy to fight against the Empire.

In [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], just as he had seen in his vision, Rahn was captured by one of the Inquisitors, [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]], and his [[Seven Dark Jedi|band]] of [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]]. Jerec, who also wanted to find the Valley in order to harness its power, probed Rahn's mind and learned about Morgan and his discovery. Having become a traitor in his own mind, Rahn aggressively attacked Jerec's Dark Jedi, but was killed by the Inquisitor himself.

Following Yoda's teachings, Rahn continued to live as a [[The Force/Legends|Force]] ghost, appearing to Kyle Katarn and instructing him to stop Jerec. Rahn also appeared to the youngest of Jerec's Dark Jedi, [[Yun]], guiding him toward the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]]. Under Rahn's guidance, Katarn killed Jerec and freed the souls of the Jedi trapped in the Valley. Yun also played his part by giving his life in order to save Katarn's.

==Biography==
===Early life===
{{Quote|I am a Jedi. And right now, that is a very dangerous thing to be.|Qu Rahn|<ref name="DF: RA audio">[[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent (audio drama)|''Dark Forces: Rebel Agent'' audio drama]]</ref>}}
[[File:Qu_rahn.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Jedi Master Qu Rahn]]
Qu Rahn was a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] born on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Socorro/Legends|Socorro]],<ref name="CSWE" /> and chosen to be [[Jedi training/Legends|trained]] as a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. As a [[Youngling/Legends|youngling]], Rahn was a member of the [[Katarn Clan]], in which he trained under [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]. Rahn grew to become an extremely loyal, steadfast Jedi,<ref name="TDFS" /> and by [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], he held the rank of [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]]. During the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], which saw many planets seceding from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], Rahn led a special joint task force of [[Judicial Department/Legends|Judicial Department]] and [[Senate Bureau of Intelligence/Legends|Senate Bureau of Intelligence]] agents investigating suspected [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] terrorist [[Gavrilonnis Tejere]], who had tried to sabotage the [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] assembly on the [[Yag'Dhul/Legends|Yag'Dhul]] Ambassadorial Landing Platform.<ref name="HNN">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|53|news/13425_1.html|Would-Be Saboteur Captured}}</ref> Rahn was active during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] that followed<ref name="CSWE" /> and was one of the few survivors of [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] and the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] initiated by [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]. Like many of the Jedi that escaped [[Death/Legends|death]], Rahn went into hiding.<ref name="HNN Special Inaugural">{{InsiderCite|84|Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:241}}</ref>

===Imperial years===
Shortly after the formation of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], he was listed as one of the Jedi fugitives by [[Imperial HoloVision]], along with [[Kai Justiss]], [[Ydra Kilwallen Sibwarra|Ydra Kilwallen]], [[Maw (Dark Jedi)|Maw]], [[Ranik Solusar]], and [[Halagad Ventor]].<ref name="HNN Special Inaugural" />

As the Purge progressed, it became known to Rahn that many Jedi, such as [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]], and Ventor, had fallen to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and, in some cases, become servants of Palpatine. Skywalker became the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] Darth Vader, and Jerec joined the [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitorius]], an organization dedicated to extermination of every last Jedi. Rahn also discovered that Yoda had survived Order 66 and was living in self-imposed exile on the planet [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]] following his [[Skirmish in the Senate|failure]] to defeat Palpatine. Later, Rahn would be part of the group of Jedi that was betrayed by Ventor to Darth Vader. Rahn, however, somehow managed to evade the Dark Lord of the Sith.<ref name="TDFS" />

Troubled and confused about how those Jedi could turn to the dark side, Rahn made the dangerous journey to Dagobah to visit Yoda. Rahn hoped that Yoda's wisdom would help to give clarity to the thoughts that were troubling him. Instead of a reassuring conversation, Yoda merely spoke enigmatically about a [[Ruusan/Legends|planet]], on which was located a "[[Valley of the Jedi|valley of Jedi souls]]," a place of great power. Yoda bestowed upon Rahn the rank of Jedi Master, giving him a gold [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] in the process and sending him on his way, but not before teaching Rahn the ability to live on after death as a [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghost]]. The new knowledge and Yoda's gift baffled Rahn, but he accepted the lightsaber and vowed to protect the weapon as it would him.<ref name="TDFS" />

===Search for the Valley of the Jedi===
{{Quote|Sorry, my friend, but the knowledge is safer with you. Much safer. I must travel. And there are those who hope to find me. Hide what you know and leave instructions for someone you trust. Those who follow the dark side would like nothing better than to find this place and use it for evil.|Rahn instructs [[Morgan Katarn]] to keep the location of the Valley of the Jedi secret|<ref name="DF: RA">''[[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent]]''</ref>}}
After his meeting with Yoda, Rahn became determined to find the Valley of the Jedi and free the spirits trapped there in order to prevent any possibility that the valley's power would be used for evil. For the next several years, Rahn searched obsessively for any information about the history or location of the valley. Time and time again, any leads Rahn found to the valley's hiding place left him empty-handed. In his mind, the valley seemed unreachable&mdash;as mythic as the planet [[Millinar]] or the [[Lost City of the Jedi]]. To make matters worse, the relentless task of the Galactic Empire's Inquisitorius to find every last Jedi made travel perilous. Ultimately, Jerec caught wind of Rahn's search. Hoping to find the valley in order to obtain its power, the Inquisitor initiated his own search. The race to be the first to find the Valley of the Jedi was on.<ref name="TDFS" />

During this time, Rahn heard a report<ref name="TDFS" /> that Halagad Ventor, the man who had caused so many Jedi deaths, had been found by a group of [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] soldiers and redeemed before he died.<ref name="Domain of Evil">''[[Domain of Evil]]''</ref> Rahn scoffed at such rumors, refusing to believe the tale that had found its way to his ears and remembering that Yoda had once told him that the dark side would forever dominate the destiny of those who had chosen it.<ref name="TDFS" />

[[File:Morgankatarn.jpg|thumb|right|160px|Morgan Katarn, briefly a friend of Rahn's]]
After countless years of dead ends and false leads, Rahn was close to admitting defeat in what was increasingly appearing to be a fruitless quest, but then a [[Force vision/Legends|vision]] helped to restore his resolve. The vision led him to a stranger named [[Morgan Katarn]], whose [[Katarn family|surname]] was [[Katarn/Legends|namesake]] of the [[Jedi_Initiate_Clan/Legends|clan]] he used to belong in his youth.<ref name="TDFS" /> Katarn was a [[Farmer/Legends|farmer]] on [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust's]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Sulon/Legends|Sulon]], and the leader of the local resistance group. In [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]] Rahn arrived on Sulon and was hosted by the farmer and his [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[WeeGee]] at the [[Katarn family compound|Katarn homestead]]. After dinner and discussing about his activities, the discussion turned to Katarn finding the Valley by chance some months ago, and a thousand-year-old [[Poem of Ages|prophecy]] that the native [[Bouncer]]s revealed to him; the [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghosts]] needed a Jedi to deliver them, and the overwhelming mystical experience tormented Katarn, who was unable to share this secret with anyone; until Rahn came to him.<ref name="DF: RA audio" />

Rahn said that he knew about that place, which held unimaginable power as a [[Vergence/Legends|Force nexus]], dangerous if it fell to the wrong side; he intended to send an expedition of experts, with Katarn as their guide, to probe and investigate the ruins; but Rahn had to go and refused to know the valley's exact location at that time, having seen in the same vision that he might be captured before he could reach it; he warned him not to inform the Alliance either, as it was full of spies. Instead Rahn urged Katarn to pass down the location of the valley (and [[Qu Rahn's lightsaber|his own lightsaber]] which entrusted to Morgan) to his own son&mdash;the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]]-in-training [[Kyle Katarn]]. Although Morgan was worried that his son had Imperial training, Rahn had sensed that Kyle was [[Force-sensitive/Legends|strong with the Force]]<ref name="TDFS" /><ref name="DF: RA" /> and his destiny was different;<ref name="DF: RA audio" /> a vision showed Rahn that Morgan's son would be the one who would unlock the secrets of the Valley.<ref name="CSWE" />

Katarn did exactly as Rahn had asked. He created and embedded a [[map to the Valley of the Jedi]] on the ceiling of his house and left instructions for Kyle on a [[Hologram disc/Legends|holodisc]], which could only be accessed through Katarn's family droid, WeeGee. A few months later, Morgan was killed by Jerec during the [[Subjugation of Sulon]], but Jerec was still oblivious to Katarn's discovery. By that time, Rahn had apparently made contact with the Rebel Alliance and its leader, [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]]; it was through him that Mothma knew about Morgan and that he was a great local leader of their cause. During her meeting with the recently defected Kyle Katarn, Mon Mothma spoke of Rahn, calling him a mutual friend and delivering Rahn's greetings to Morgan's son.<ref name="DF: SftE" />

===Confrontation with Jerec===
{{Quote|Why hesitate? Strike me down.''"<br />"''In time, Rahn. First, I need something from you.|Qu Rahn and Jerec aboard the ''Vengeance''|<ref name="DF II" />}}
[[File:Jerec-QuRahn_DFJK.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Jerec rips information from Qu Rahn's mind.]]
In [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], one year after the Rebel Alliance [[Battle of Endor/Legends|had dealt a massive blow]] to the Galactic Empire on the forest moon of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]],<ref name="ERC" /> Rahn led a team of Rebel Alliance agents&mdash;a young [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] named [[Duno Dree]]; the female wire-thin weapons expert [[Cee Norley]]; and [[Rolanda Gron]], a [[Klatooinian/Legends|Klatooinian]] technologist&mdash;to the planet [[Dorlo]]. Their [[Mission to Dorlo|mission]] was to find the linguistics expert [[Nij Por Ral]], who was working at an excavation site there, and convince him to join Rahn's group. Arriving on Dorlo in a [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]], the Rebels rode a [[Skimmer/Legends|skimmer]] to the site of Por Ral's work, where they were able to convince the linguist to join them.<ref name="DF: RA" />

Having acquired Por Ral, however, they faced opposition from a group of stormtroopers led by three Dark Jedi<ref name="DF: RA audio" />&mdash;the former Jedi Maw,<ref name="The Dark Forces Saga 4">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050526a|series=The Dark Forces Saga|text=Part 4: Of the Crudest Matter}}</ref> the [[Prophets of the Dark Side|Prophetess of the Dark Side]] [[Sariss]], and the young [[Epicanthix]] [[Yun]]<ref name="The Dark Forces Saga 3">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050512b|series=The Dark Forces Saga|text=Part 3: Pride of the Dark Side}}</ref>&mdash;who had been sent by Jerec to capture Rahn. Rahn and the Rebels decided to try to reach their corvette in order to escape from the Dark Jedi. Rahn told his group not to use the skimmer, fearing that the Imperials might spot its heat signature; instead, he ordered them to set out to the corvette on foot.<ref name="DF: RA audio" /> However, Maw had the unique ability to sense others' fear. He spotted Rahn's group and soon the Imperials, riding skimmers themselves, started gaining on them. To buy the Rebels some time, Rahn formulated a plan that included Norley remaining behind with a [[Missile launcher/Legends|rocket launcher]]. She managed to destroy one of the two skimmers, but was killed after doing so. However, her sacrifice bought some time for Rahn, Dree, Gron, and Por Ral to reach the [[Starship/Legends|starship]]. Dree managed to pilot the corvette off the planet, destroying Jerec's remaining skimmer in the process, although not managing to kill its crew of Dark Jedi.<ref name="DF: RA" />

Once in [[Realspace/Legends|space]], the corvette was caught in the [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] of the [[Vengeance (Vengeance-class)|''Vengeance'']], Jerec's personal battleship. An assault [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] then docked with the corvette, carrying another of Jerec's Dark Jedi, [[Boc Aseca|Boc]]. The Rebels were asked to surrender, but did not comply. In response, the Imperials filled the corvette with [[coma gas]]. Rahn and his group tried to reach for [[Environment suit/Legends|space suits]], but fell prey to the effects of the gas. Unconscious, they were transferred first to the shuttle and then to the ''Vengeance''. The corvette itself was used for target practice by the ''Vengeance''{{'s}} artillery crew.<ref name="DF: RA" /><ref name="DF: RA audio" />

Rahn soon awoke from the effects of the gas, only to find two more Dark Jedi&mdash;[[Gorc]] and [[Picaroon C. Boodle|Pic]]&mdash;staring at him. Rahn tried to reach for his lightsaber, but found out that Pic had taken Yoda's gift. Rahn and his companions were then escorted to the ''Vengeance''{{'s}} [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]], where they faced Jerec and all of his Dark Jedi. Jerec began questioning Rahn about the valley, but the Jedi Master refused to answer, so Jerec ordered his men to kill Rahn's comrades. One by one, Gron, Por Ral, and Dree were killed, but Qu Rahn still did not answer, even after being beaten to his knees by the Dark Jedi. Rahn attempted to will himself to die and asked Jerec to strike him down. Instead of killing Rahn, Jerec used the Force to [[Drain Knowledge|rip the information]] he needed about the Valley of the Jedi from his mind. The Dark Jedi discovered that Morgan Katarn, the man he had killed years ago, knew the whereabouts of the valley and had left the coordinates somewhere on his farm.<ref name="DF: RA" />

[[File:Rahn_fighting.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Rahn makes his last stand aboard the ''Vengeance''.]]
Rahn was devastated; in his own mind, he had become the very thing he had despised&mdash;a betrayer of the Jedi. Not only had he lost Yoda's lightsaber, but he had betrayed Morgan Katarn and a secret that had been kept for generations. In that moment, the Jedi Master, gave into despair and, using [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinesis]], he stole Yun's lightsaber and attacked his captors. Rahn put up a valiant fight, with Jerec's followers proving unable to land a single blow on him. Rahn managed to injure Boc and [[Sai tok/Legends|sever]] Maw in half at the waist, only to be brought to his knees by a [[Force blast]] from Jerec. As Jerec moved in for the kill, Yoda's voice echoed in Rahn's head the promise that one day he would understand. At that moment, Jerec struck the killing blow, [[Sai cha/Legends|decapitating]] the helpless Jedi Master. However, in his final moments of life, Rahn saw the spirits of Anakin Skywalker and Halagad Ventor, two Jedi that he knew that had fallen to the dark side many years back, and yet were eventually redeemed, and finally realized what Yoda had wanted him to understand; that no one was beyond redemption.<ref name="DF II" /><ref name="TDFS" /><ref name="DF: RA" />

===The spirit of Rahn===
{{Quote|A crossroads lies before you.&hellip;The same man who murdered your father contemplates an even greater evil. His name is Jerec, and he seeks a place called the Valley of the Jedi, a place where thousands of Jedi spirits are trapped, a place of almost unbelievable power, a place he must never reach. Because if he does - the results could be catastrophic. Imagine someone who could destroy a star with a whisper, eradicate a solar system with a snap of his fingers, or 'think' a planet from its orbit.|Qu Rahn, to Kyle Katarn|<ref name="DF: RA" />}}
[[File:RahnsGuidance-HaL.jpg|thumb|left|210px|Qu Rahn, appearing in a vision to Kyle Katarn]]
Even after his physical death, Rahn was successful to transcend the physical plane and lived on as a Force ghost, as he had been taught by Yoda years earlier. Meanwhile, having acquired the information he needed from Rahn's mind, Jerec hired the droid information broker [[8t88/Legends|8t88]], who found Morgan's [[Hologram disc/Legends|holodisk]] on Sulon. Being unable to decipher it, the droid arranged a meeting with Kyle Katarn on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]]. Katarn refused to cooperate and was attacked by several [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] hired by 8t88. Rahn was watching over Morgan's son for some time, and in times of need he guided him on how to use the Force, in this manner helping evade death and obtain the disk from 8t88. While Katarn was recovering from [[Mission to Nar Shaddaa (5 ABY)|that encounter]] on board the ''[[Mercy (hospital ship)|Mercy]]'', Rahn appeared to him in a dream, telling Katarn about the Valley of the Jedi and Jerec's plans. He informed him that his fate was bound to that of his father, and the Valley; he was already training him to the ways of the Jedi, and that the disk would help him to master them, and reach the Valley.<ref name="DF II" /><ref name="DF: RA" />

Guided by Rahn, Katarn returned to his home on Sulon, where he found Rahn's lightsaber and decoded the disc, learning about the stone map embedded on the ceiling. He soon discovered, however, that the map had been taken to [[Government House (Sulon)|Jerec's palace]] in the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Barons Hed]], where it was to be deciphered by 8t88. As soon as he reached the city, Katarn was attacked by a [[Unidentified female thief (Sulon)|female bounty hunter]] with a [[Remote/Legends|remote]]. Rahn once again contacted Katarn, helping him to familiarize himself with the newly acquired lightsaber. With Rahn's guidance, Katarn was able to defeat both the woman and her remote. As a disembodied voice, Rahn contacted Katarn several more times, providing Morgan's son with information on Jerec's Dark Jedi. Despite Katarn's efforts, however, Jerec discovered that the valley was located on the planet Ruusan. Soon, his forces reached the planet and began excavation works at the valley.<ref name="DF II" /><ref name="DF: RA" />

Rahn's spirit followed Katarn as he arrived on Ruusan, and as he was landing on the planet with the ''[[Moldy Crow/Legends|Moldy Crow]]'', he heard Rahn's voice again, warning him not to give in to hate.<ref name="DF: JK audio" />

Sensing that there was something good left in the youngest of Jerec's Dark Jedi, Yun, Rahn contacted him on Ruusan. Yun had been tasked by Jerec with getting rid of the Jedi and Sith spirits that roamed around the valley; he tried to defeat them by shaping the Force and hurling it towards them, but did not succeed. Rahn appeared as a voice in the young darksider's head and advised Yun to try another tactic&mdash;to sense the spirits' pain. Yun followed Rahn's advice and was able to make the spirits depart, and Rahn then explained that Yun would play an important part in the events that would follow. The Epicanthix asked what part, and Rahn answered that it was entirely up to him.<ref name="DF: JK" /><ref name="DF: JK audio" /> The encounter with Rahn made such a deep impression on Yun that several days later, when a [[Groundquake/Legends|groundquake]] caused a rock to fall on an Imperial called [[Jaru]], he used the light side of the Force to help him. After that, Rahn appeared to Yun again, telling him that the dark side was not the only source of power.<ref name="DF: JK" />

Meanwhile Katarn managed to approach Jerec, and he was closer than ever; Katarn was riding a [[turbolift/Legends|turbolift]] of his tower, frightened with the idea of direct confrontation with him alone. Then Rahn spoke again, ensuring that he, and the Force, was with Katarn, and not displaying extreme self-confidence was only a sign of his strength. Rahn advised Kyle to use his name to his advantage when he meets the "half-man" who was about to meet soon; referring to Maw who was expecting Katarn on a nearby platform. Indeed, Maw was enraged when Katarn mentioned Rahn's name, the man who cut Maw in half.<ref name="DF: JK" />

Katarn killed Maw in anger and confronted Jerec near the Dark Jedi's cargo ship, the ''[[Sulon Star]]''. There, Jerec offered Katarn the chance to join his cadre. Although he had been driven close to the dark side by Maw's [[Dun Möch/Legends|taunts]], Katarn was able to hold off his ambition and refuse. In response, Jerec pushed him into the ''Sulon Star'' and sent the ship crashing towards the surface. Rahn helped Katarn evade death by telling him that Kyle's ship, the ''[[Moldy Crow/Legends|Moldy Crow]]'', had been kept in the hangar bay of the ''Sulon Star''.<ref name="DF II" /><ref name="DF: JK" /> Katarn managed to escape the doomed ''Sulon Star'', but could not handle the controls of his own ship and crashed the ''Moldy Crow'' near the valley and lay unconscoius in pain.<ref name="DF II" /><ref name="DF: JK" /> As his mind was connected to the Force, Rahn's vision appeared to him again, and wanted to show him how the present was connected to the past: in the vision Kyle became the alter-ego of the Jedi [[Tal (Jedi)|Tal]] and the Dark Jedi [[LaTor]], witnessing their final moves before Kaan's [[thought bomb]].<ref name="DF: JK" /> 

He was found, unconscious, by Boc, Sariss, and Yun. Before leaving to assist Jerec, Boc crushed the lightsaber that had once belonged to Rahn with a rock. Sariss then moved in for the kill, but Yun, driven close to the light side by Rahn, blocked her blow. Sariss deflected her lightsaber into Yun himself. Before dying, Yun told her that Katarn, as a Jedi, deserved a battle.<ref name="DF II" /> This way, he was redeemed and returned to the light side.<ref name="DF: JK" /><ref name="DF: JK audio" />

[[File:Statues.jpg|thumb|250px|The statues of Qu Rahn and Morgan Katarn]]
Katarn picked up Yun's lightsaber and killed Sariss. He then proceeded further and confronted Boc and his [[Jar'Kai/Legends|double lightsabers]]; it was Rahn who reminded Kyle that his mind is also a weapon, although this led him to use the dark side [[Darkshear]] against Boc.<ref name="DF: JK" />

It was the second time Katarn used the dark side, and right then he faced Jerec, who was in possession of the valley's power. During this confrontation Katarn nearly fell to the dark side due to his hatred and thirst for revenge, and wanted to ignore Rahn who tried to help, even reminding to him the lesson of compassion learned by Yun, and that his hatred only made Jerec stronger; in the end he managed to hold off, and instead of attacking Jerec, destroying himself, he used a [[Force Light|shield of light]] to protect both of them from the dark side.<ref name="DF: JK" /><ref name="DF: JK audio" /> This led to Jerec's death, after which the spirits that had been trapped inside the valley were finally freed.<ref name="DF II" /><ref name="DF: JK audio">[[Dark Forces: Jedi Knight (audio drama)|''Dark Forces: Jedi Knight'' audio drama]]</ref> To honor Rahn's memory and that of his father, Katarn carved their images in the two statues near the entrance to the valley.<ref name="DF II" /> After the events on Ruusan, Qu Rahn was not seen or heard contacting Katarn.

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|A wonderful gentleman. Your father thought very highly of him.|[[WeeGee]] tells about Rahn to Kyle Katarn|<ref name="DF: RA" />}}
[[File:Rahns_lightsaber.png|thumb|left|250px|Rahn's lightsaber, which he passed on to Kyle Katarn]]
Rahn was a [[Color/Legends|dark]]-skinned man with black [[Hair/Legends|hair]] and brown [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="DF: JK" /> Although raised as an extremely loyal Jedi, he was sometimes haunted by thoughts of vengeance and hatred. He was deeply troubled by the actions of Jedi traitors and considered that such turncoats like Jerec, Anakin Skywalker, and Halagad Ventor had sealed their own fates&mdash;they could never be saved. Not even knowing most of them, Rahn truly hated those who had betrayed the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. Sometimes, Rahn almost hoped that Jerec would find him so that he could exact justice on the Inquisitor. When Jerec ripped information about Morgan Katarn from Rahn's mind, the Jedi Master believed that he had become a traitor to the Order himself. At that moment, he gave into despair and attacked Jerec's Dark Jedi in anger. However, immediately before his death, Rahn realized that he had been wrong in his beliefs as he glimpsed the spirits of the redeemed Ventor and Skywalker. Rahn finally understood that Yoda wanted him to see that no one was beyond redemption. This understanding led Rahn to appear to Yun, helping the young darksider to turn to the light.<ref name="TDFS" /><ref name="DF: JK" />

Following his meeting with Yoda on Dagobah, Rahn became obsessed with finding the Valley of the Jedi. This obsession led him to many years of passionate search and, ultimately, to his demise at the hands of Jerec. However, it also made Rahn's meeting with Morgan Katarn possible. During the brief period that he stayed at Katarn's farm, Rahn and Katarn became good friends. Rahn was also on good terms with the Rebel Alliance leader, Mon Mothma.<ref name="TDFS" /><ref name="DF: RA" />

When not searching for the valley, Rahn spent a lot of time in contemplation, eventually realizing that there were worse things than death. He possessed a journal, where he wrote his thoughts regarding the Force, Jerec, and Jerec's Dark Jedi.<ref name="DF II" /> After Rahn's death, Kyle Katarn inherited that journal, and he often consulted its wisdom in order to better understand the ways of the Force. Rahn was a kind and wise individual, and those traits could be easily seen in him by others.<ref name="CSWE" /> Nevertheless, the Jedi was a strong-willed man, able to leave Cee Norley behind, fully realizing that she would be killed. After that, he refused to tell anything to Jerec, even after being beaten and forced to watch as his comrades were killed one by one. When it was Duno Dree's turn, Rahn displayed his leadership qualities by turning to the frightened young man and willing him to die in order to protect the valley's secret.<ref name="DF: RA" />

Rahn liked to say that "Opportunity dwells within disaster", something that Morgan Katarn remembered during the [[Subjugation of Sulon]].<ref name="DF: SftE" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|My path is the dark one. But if the Force is with me, I will find light at the other end.|Qu Rahn|<ref name="DF: RA audio" />}}
A fully-trained Jedi recognized as a Jedi Master by Yoda himself, Rahn was skilled with both the Force and the lightsaber, being able to single-handedly defeat five of Jerec's minions and severely wound one of them. For the most part, however, Rahn preferred to [[Jedi Consular|concentrate on his Force abilities]]. He was capable in telekinesis, which he demonstrated by stealing Yun's lightsaber from his belt. In addition, Rahn knew [[Force speed/Legends|Force speed]], and was one of the few Jedi to appear as a Force ghost, having been taught this secret by Yoda.<ref name="DF II" /><ref name="TDFS" /> Rahn drew on the Light Side of the Force; in the presence of Jerec and the Dark Jedi, he [[Force Light|"wrapped" himself]] in some white-Force cloak, causing the concentration of evil around him to retreat.<ref name="DF: RA" />

Rahn's [[Force sense/Legends|Force sense]] ability was especially developed, to the point that it even allowed him to see the future. It was a vision that led him to Morgan Katarn, and in the same vision, Rahn foresaw that he would be captured. Never meeting Kyle Katarn in person, Rahn sensed that Morgan's son was very strong in the Force and that his path was different from the one he had initially chosen<ref name="TDFS" /> and had a premonition showing him that Kyle would play a key role in finding the Valley.<ref name="CSWE" /> When he met Jerec in person on the bridge of the ''Vengeance'', he felt a concentration of evil, and the Force churning due to the Dark Jedi's thoughts and actions.<ref name="DF: RA" /> After becoming a ghost, Rahn foretold that Yun would play an important part in the events on Ruusan.<ref name="DF: JK" />

Rahn could write, read, and speak two languages, his native [[Socorran (language)/Legends|Socorran]] and [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], and was skilled in [[Computer/Legends|computer]] use, some simple weapons, and martial arts. He also had some knowledge of how to treat injuries.<ref name="TDFS" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Dark_Rahn.jpg|thumb|right|150px|The "Dark Rahn"]]
Qu Rahn first appeared in the [[1997]] [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]'', where he was portrayed by [[Bennet Guillory]]. Rahn appeared twice in the game&mdash;first in the introductory cutscene, where he was killed by Jerec, and then as a ghost in Katarn's dream. His voice guided the main protagonist throughout the rest of the game.<ref name="DF II" /> Rahn later appeared in the [[1998]] novella adaptations of the game&mdash;''[[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent]]''<ref name="DF: RA" /> and ''[[Dark Forces: Jedi Knight]]''<ref name="DF: JK" />&mdash;and, subsequently, in the [[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent (audio drama)|audio drama]] [[Dark Forces: Jedi Knight (audio drama)|adaptations]] of the two novellas. In the audio dramas, [[Michael Tezla]] portrayed Rahn.<ref name="Dark Forces: The Collector's Trilogy">''[[Dark Forces: The Collector's Trilogy]]'' audio drama''</ref> Rahn was also mentioned in the first installment of the [[Star Wars: Dark Forces (novellas)|''Dark Forces'' trilogy]], [[Dark Forces: Soldier for the Empire|''Soldier for the Empire'']],<ref name="DF: SftE" /> and its [[Dark Forces: Soldier for the Empire (audio drama)|audio drama]] adaptation.<ref name="Soldier audio">[[Dark Forces: Soldier for the Empire (audio drama)|''Dark Forces: Soldier for the Empire'' audio drama]]</ref> Rahn's backstory was expanded in ''[[The Dark Forces Saga]]'', a series of game scenarios released by [[Wizards of the Coast]] on their [[Wizards.com|web site]].<ref name="TDFS" />

Rahn was listed among the surviving Jedi in the [[Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:241|Special Edition]] of [[HoloNet News (Insider)|HoloNet News]], published in the [[Star Wars Insider 84|84th]] issue of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine.<ref name="HNN Special Inaugural" /> Rahn's image was originally going to appear in ''Insider'' but it was instead made into another Jedi, [[Koffi Arana]].<ref name="Blog-joecorroney|22">{{Blog|joecorroney|22|Mr. Hammond, HoloNet News is back online! (sort of&hellip;)}}</ref> In an interview published in the ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II: The Official Strategy Guide]]'', the lead writer of the game, [[Justin Chin]], presents a slightly different backstory for Rahn, which contradicts his later portrayal. According to Chin, in his youth, Rahn was a wanderer and "sort of" an orphan, instead of a loyal steadfast student as described in more recent sources. Chin also states that at some point during his search for the Valley, Rahn ran into Jerec, who attempted to recruit him into his cadre. Although Rahn was somewhat borderline between the light and the dark sides, he refused the offer. As none of this information was published elsewhere outside of the interview, this article gives precedence to more recent sources.<ref name="JK Guide">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II: The Official Strategy Guide]]''</ref>

In ''Dark Forces II: Jedi Knight'', he only appears as Rahn. The first name Qu is given only in the game's manual. The multiplayer feature of ''Dark Forces II'' has a model named "Dark Rahn" among its playable characters. This "Dark Rahn" wears pants and a jacket, and his face is covered in white tattoos.<ref name="DF II" /> The same model is available in ''Jedi Knight''{{'s}} expansion pack, ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Mysteries of the Sith]]''.<ref name="MotS">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Mysteries of the Sith]]''</ref> Rahn's name is misspelled "Qu Rhan" in HoloNet News.<ref name="HNN" /> Rahn was also mentioned in the [http://wizards.com/default.asp?x=starwars/article/KyleKatarn online preview] of the [[Jedi Academy (Star Wars Miniatures)|''Jedi Academy'' set]] of [[Star Wars Miniatures]]. The preview features a continuity error, as it states that it was the spirit of Rahn who informed Kyle Katarn of his father's affiliation with the Rebel Alliance. Katarn's discovery of Morgan's Rebel sympathies, however, is featured in ''Soldier for the Empire'', which takes place several years prior to Rahn's contact with Kyle.<ref name="Preview">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/KyleKatarn|text=''Jedi Academy'' Miniatures Preview 5}}</ref>

===Non-canon ending===
{{Quote|For you, the choice is the dark side. Forever will it dominate your destiny.|Qu Rahn, to Kyle Katarn, before leaving him|audio=QuRahn-DarkSide.flac|<ref name="DF II" />}}
In the non-canon ending of ''Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II'', where Kyle Katarn chooses the dark side path, Rahn abandons him during the crash of the ''Sulon Star''. Still, Katarn survives and becomes the new Emperor after killing Jerec and absorbing the valley's power. It is possible, however, to have Rahn say the above line to Katarn much earlier in the game. This event can be triggered at the start of level four if Katarn chooses to destroy his family droid WeeGee, although Rahn continues to guide Katarn as normal, and the player can still attain the light side ending afterward.<ref name="DF II" />

===Differences between versions===
''Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II'', the ''Dark Forces'' novellas, their audio dramatizations, and ''The Dark Forces Saga'' scenarios are all different in a number of ways and sometimes provide conflicting information. Apart from minor dialogue changes, the most notable difference is the depiction of Rahn's death scene in the audio dramatization. Unlike the game and the novel, Rahn does not attack the Dark Jedi in it; instead, he begs Morgan Katarn to forgive him. Additionally, there is some inconsistency over Rahn's part in Jerec's defeat. Both the game and the ''Jedi Knight'' novel depict Katarn not responding to Jerec's taunts. The audio drama, however, shows Katarn giving in to anger and almost turning to the dark side, and only thanks to Rahn's help, he manages to hold off.<ref name="DF: JK audio" /> ''The Dark Forces Saga'' also implies that Rahn has foreseen his capture by Jerec.<ref name="TDFS" /> On the other hand, ''Rebel Agent'' makes no mention of such vision. Instead, Rahn intends to gather a team to study the valley and free the spirits all by himself.<ref name="DF: RA" />
